clue.text: Beak's opening - key extracted from our French trial

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out, so the named letter is taken away from the word that follows

blocks.note: nos is French for 'our' before a plural noun
A is a musical key
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird's bill gets a curious mention in a French court case.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's 'ex tract' is a split of 'extracted'. A beak is a nose, here a bird's, so its opening is the nostril.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is an external opening of the nose, and a beak is jocular slang for a nose.

clue.text: The idea is to get it back in the middle of the day

indicators.note: getting something back here means turning it round so it reads the other way
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: noon is twelve o'clock, midday
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plan to recover something by lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a thought or concept, which is what an idea is.

clue.text: Real estate includes no such outlandish castle

definitions.text: Real estate includes no such outlandish castle
definitions.note: the answer is the adjective in 'castle in Spain', i.e. a Spanish castle

blocks.clueFragment: Real estate includes no such outlandish castle
blocks.note: surface reading: no property portfolio has a castle this bizarre
setter's reading: a castle in a foreign land that exists only in daydreams, so it is never real estate

explanation.surface: No property on the market includes a castle this weird.
explanation.walkthrough: A castle in Spain is an idiom for a daydream or fanciful plan, so it is not real estate at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles in Spain are imaginary schemes, so a Spanish castle is foreign and unreal, never genuine property.

clue.text: One or two girls for the musical

blocks.note: surface reading: a single girl or a pair
setter's reading: the title can be read as one double name or as two girls' names side by side

explanation.surface: Casting one or two young women for a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose-Marie is a 1924 operetta; its title is one name, or the two names Rose and Marie.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose-Marie is a Friml and Stothart musical set in the Canadian Rockies, later a famous film.

clue.text: Its findings are not reliable

blocks.note: surface reading: an untrustworthy investigation or test
setter's reading: what this machine finds are untruths, so its discoveries are by definition false statements

explanation.surface: Criticism of a dubious inquiry or test.
explanation.walkthrough: The device is notoriously unreliable, and what it seeks to find are falsehoods: both readings work.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie detector, or polygraph, is a machine meant to find falsehoods, and its results are famously doubtful.

clue.text: The measure of a loafer?

blocks.note: surface reading: the size of an idler, or of a slip-on shoe
setter's reading: something that makes loaves, so its measure is a dimension with bread in it

explanation.surface: How do you size up a lazy person, or a slip-on shoe?
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as BREAD plus TH, so a 'loafer' is read as something made of loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is width, one of the measurements of any object, and it begins with bread.

clue.text: There's not much to be got from arbitration

indicators.note: getting something out of a word means taking a run of letters from inside it

blocks.note: letters two to four of the word

explanation.surface: Going to arbitration rarely gets you much.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit is a small amount, so not much.

clue.text: What the May Queen wanted to be called

definitions.text: What the May Queen wanted to be called

blocks.clueFragment: What the May Queen wanted to be called
blocks.note: surface reading: the title or name the girl wanted
setter's reading: woken, as in Tennyson's poem where she asks her mother to wake her in good time

explanation.surface: The name a festival queen hoped to be given.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's poem The May Queen has the refrain 'You must wake and call me early, call me early, mother dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's May Queen asks to be woken at an early hour, so 'call' means rouse, not name.

clue.text: Let out, a number of Romans indulge

blocks.note: three Roman numerals, D, I and V, run together
taken as written

explanation.surface: A collection of Romans were allowed out to enjoy themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue gives no signal for dropping IND from indulge; the letters may stand in for it. The answer is certain from definition and crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: To divulge a secret is to let it out, revealing what was hidden.

clue.text: Novel written for itself, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: a Victorian novel by Charles Reade, published 1863
second meaning: what a cheque made out to 'Cash' or 'Self' turns into, actual notes and coins

explanation.walkthrough: Hard Cash is Charles Reade's 1863 novel; the second half is loose, a cheque written payable to 'Cash' being exchanged for real money.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cash means physical money, as distinct from cheques, and is also the title of a Charles Reade book.

clue.text: Somehow entrant is passing

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newcomer is somehow just going by.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient and passing both describe something brief that does not last.

clue.text: Tweed, for example, might suit fishermen

blocks.clueFragment: Tweed, for example, might suit fishermen
blocks.note: surface reading: tweed cloth makes good clothing for anglers
setter's reading: the Tweed is a flowing stretch of water, and it suits anglers because of its salmon

explanation.surface: Tweed jackets are just the thing for anglers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tweed is a cloth, but also the river on the border of England and Scotland, famous for salmon fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is an example of a watercourse, a famous salmon stream on the Scottish border.

clue.text: Hatred drives quiet leader from platform

indicators.note: driving something from a place forces it out, so a letter is removed from the next word

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical instruction for quiet, and it leads off the word
a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: A speaker who is shouted down and forced off the stage by hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is widespread hatred or disgust directed at someone.

clue.text: Going round in circles

blocks.note: surface reading: getting nowhere, repeating oneself fruitlessly
setter's reading: literal motion along a small circle whose centre rides on a larger one

explanation.surface: Someone getting nowhere in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: An epicycle is a circle moving on another circle, as in old models of the planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicyclic describes motion in an epicycle, a small orbit carried round a larger orbit, as in planetary gearing.

clue.text: Mark of tomahawk ruined Indian tent? Nothing in it

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so its letters are rearranged
in it says the item is placed inside the tent before the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A hatchet blow leaves a mark on a wrecked wigwam with nothing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The tomahawk and Indian tent belong to the same Wild West scene, which hides that the tent is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An indentation is a notch or dent, the kind of mark a hatchet blow leaves in wood.

clue.text: Author cooks children's cakes

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A writer who also bakes treats for the young.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens was the Victorian novelist who wrote Oliver Twist and Great Expectations.

clue.text: It doesn't pay him to mind his own business

definitions.text: It doesn't pay him to mind his own business

blocks.clueFragment: It doesn't pay him to mind his own business
blocks.note: surface reading: a busybody who cannot stop meddling
setter's reading: look after, and he is paid to look after other people's property

explanation.surface: A nosy person who profits from meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind your own business' sounds like a rebuke; here mind means look after, and his wages come from minding others'.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker is employed to look after a building or premises that belong to someone else.

clue.text: It might be Bob's turn to intractable

indicators.note: 'it might be' says the answer is one possible version of the words that follow, rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Bob being difficult when it's his go.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed text reads oddly ('turn to intractable'); 'to' is best taken as joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn and intractable both describe someone obstinate who will not be managed or persuaded.

clue.text: The opposite of a winning way?

definitions.text: The opposite of a winning way?

blocks.clueFragment: The opposite of a winning way?
blocks.note: surface reading: an unattractive manner, the reverse of charm
setter's reading: a route, and the losers are the ones who take it

explanation.surface: What is the reverse of a charming manner?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning way' suggests charm; read it as a path, and the path of those who lost is the beaten one.
explanation.definitionFit: The beaten track is a well-worn, ordinary route, and 'beaten' is also what losers are.

clue.text: It's a mistake to put it in writing

definitions.text: It's a mistake to put it in writing

blocks.clueFragment: It's a mistake to put it in writing
blocks.note: surface reading: advice never to commit something to paper
setter's reading: the thing is itself a mistake, one found in print

explanation.surface: A warning never to commit something to paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing or writing, often listed on a correction slip in a book.

clue.text: A celestial type of white

blocks.note: surface reading: a heavenly whiteness, like a cloud or star
setter's reading: from the Celestial Empire, an old name for China

explanation.surface: A heavenly shade of white.
explanation.walkthrough: Celestial was a nineteenth-century word for Chinese, from the Celestial Empire; Chinese white is a watercolour pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese white is a zinc oxide paint, and Celestial once meant from the Celestial Empire of China.

clue.text: Island wear in stock

blocks.note: first meaning: the largest of the Channel Islands
second meaning: a knitted pullover

explanation.surface: A shop has holiday clothing from the islands available.
explanation.walkthrough: A third sense hides in 'in stock': a Jersey is a breed of dairy cattle, i.e. livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is a Channel Island, and a jersey is a knitted top named after it; the cow breed comes from there too.

clue.text: Song with two sailors back in Gilbertian kingdom

blocks.note: a tar and an AB (able seaman) are both sailors
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A number sung by a pair of seamen in a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Barataria is the island kingdom ruled jointly by the two gondoliers in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers.
explanation.definitionFit: W. S. Gilbert invented the realm of Barataria for The Gondoliers, so it is a kingdom of his making.

clue.text: One is in a revolution in Italy

definitions.note: the answer is a city, a place in that country

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a turn is one revolution, a full rotation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in an Italian uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests political upheaval but is a single rotation here. The definition names a place found in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in Piedmont, north-west Italy, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Thus Tom might take some beating

definitions.text: Thus Tom might take some beating

blocks.clueFragment: Thus Tom might take some beating
blocks.note: surface reading: a boy or a tomcat in line for punishment
setter's reading: the word said two times names a drum, which is struck

explanation.surface: A naughty boy called Tom is in for a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: Say Tom two times and you have the tom-tom, a drum played with the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Twice means two times, and a doubled tom is the tom-tom drum, which exists to be struck.

clue.text: Extremely successful shot? Not really

blocks.note: surface reading: a superb hit

explanation.surface: Was that a brilliant shot? Not really.
explanation.walkthrough: In target shooting and archery the outer is the outermost ring, so a shot there succeeds only at the extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: An outer is a shot striking the outermost scoring ring of a target, a hit but a poor one.

clue.text: Criminal trait not a good quality in a Head

definitions.text: not a good quality in a Head

blocks.note: first meaning: crooks are proverbially thick as thieves, close together

blocks.clueFragment: not a good quality in a Head
blocks.note: second meaning: a head teacher should not be stupid

explanation.surface: A dishonest streak is the last thing you want in a headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Head with a capital letter suggests a head teacher; the second sense is a dense skull, i.e. stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickness means stupidity, unwelcome in a head, and also the closeness of conspirators who are thick as thieves.

clue.text: Article from ambassador printed under Times leader

clue.text: Someone wants him to get on

definitions.text: Someone wants him to get on

blocks.clueFragment: Someone wants him to get on

setter's reading: be elected or appointed, as wanted by whoever put his name forward

clue.text: This man is not a baby farmer

definitions.text: This man is not a baby farmer
definitions.note: the answer is the 'this' that goes before 'man'

blocks.clueFragment: This man is not a baby farmer
blocks.note: surface reading: a man denying he takes in infants for money
setter's reading: put the answer before 'man' to name a grower of young plants, not of infants

explanation.surface: A man protesting that he does not take in babies for payment.
explanation.walkthrough: A baby farmer was a Victorian who took in infants for pay; a nurseryman raises young plants instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseryman grows seedlings in a plant nursery, and a nursery is also a room for babies, hence the denial.
